changelog.change: Initial entry — contemporary (Zhang) labor curve, arrest definitions, cesarean-prevention thresholds, Bishop score.

summary: Contemporary labor is slower than the old Friedman curves — the active phase is now defined from 6 cm, not 4 cm. Latent-phase arrest is NOT an indication for cesarean. Meet the explicit active-phase and second-stage arrest thresholds before calling dystocia.

rows: < 20 h nulliparous; < 14 h multiparous — variable, slow cervical change
up to 3 h without epidural; 4 h with epidural
up to 2 h without epidural; 3 h with epidural

items: Active-phase arrest: ≥ 6 cm with ruptured membranes AND no cervical change for ≥ 4 h with adequate contractions, OR ≥ 6 h with inadequate contractions.
Second-stage arrest: no descent or rotation past the durations above.
Latent-phase arrest alone is NOT an indication for cesarean — allow more time, hydration, rest, and oxytocin.
Do not diagnose failed induction until oxytocin has run ≥ 12–18 h after membrane rupture with no cervical change.
Offer operative vaginal delivery (by a skilled operator) before cesarean for a prolonged second stage.
A category-I tracing with slow but progressive labor is not dystocia.
Score ≥ 8 — favourable; induction likely to succeed without a ripening agent.
Score < 6 — unfavourable; use a cervical-ripening agent first (see the induction reference).
